hints: Look carefully at which scale is which. The bottom scale numbered 10 to 100 is the eyepiece graticule, the top scale with only a few long marks is the stage micrometer. Find two points where the lines line up exactly, at about 25 and 79.
Remember the calibration rule: real stage distance divided by number of eyepiece units. Count how many stage intervals and how many eyepiece units are covered between those two lining-up points.
walkthrough:
**Identify the two scales**

Think like a microscopist. The stage micrometer has a known size, each division is $0.1 \text{ mm}$. The eyepiece graticule has unknown arbitrary units numbered 10, 20, 30 and so on.

In the view, the top line with 3 long ticks is the stage, the bottom detailed scale is the eyepiece.

**Find the overlap and count**

Choose points where both scales line up sharply. The first stage mark lines up at about 25 eyepiece units. The third stage mark lines up at about 79 eyepiece units.

Eyepiece units covered:
$$79 - 25 = 54 \text{ eyepiece units}$$

Stage intervals covered: from first to third mark is 2 intervals.
$$2 \times 0.1 \text{ mm} = 0.2 \text{ mm}$$

**Calibrate one eyepiece unit and choose units**

One eyepiece unit equals total real distance divided by number of eyepiece units.
$$\text{1 eyepiece unit} = \frac{0.2}{54} \text{ mm}$$

Cell sizes are normally given in micrometres, $\mu m$. Since $1 \text{ mm} = 1000 \text{ } \mu m$, multiply by 1000.
$$\frac{0.2}{54} \times 1000 \text{ } \mu m$$

That is exactly row C.

options.A: Incorrect. It uses only 27 eyepiece units and divides by 1000, which would convert to metres, not keep mm. Calibration must use the full 54 units and multiply to get to smaller units.
options.B: Incorrect. It uses 52 eyepiece units and only 0.1 mm. The correct overlap is 2 stage divisions (0.2 mm) covering 54 eyepiece units from 25 to 79.
options.C: Correct. 2 stage divisions equal 0.2 mm and cover 54 eyepiece units, so (0.2 / 54) x 1000 gives the calibration in um.
options.D: Incorrect. It uses 79 eyepiece units measured from zero instead of the aligned interval of 54, and nm is far too small a unit for light microscope calibration.
